title: Optimal Stratified Allocation for Rare-Event Onset Forecasting in Dependent Sequences
abstract: arXiv:2609.04420v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Let a finite population of n labelled examples carry a class-weighted loss, with pi*n in a rare positive class weighted by N0/N1. We study estimation of total risk from a subsample K << n under designs allocating K0 and K1 draws to the two strata.   We derive the exact finite-population variance of the weighted risk estimator under class-conditional sampling without replacement and solve for the optimal allocation. The class multiplier inflates positive-stratum dispersion by the imbalance ratio, causing that ratio to cancel from the optimal allocation and making equal, rather than proportional, allocation the natural default. Simple random sampling is dominated by an explicit between-stratum term; an exact bias identity shows that cluster-representative selection has no general unbiasedness guarantee; and a Serfling bound transfers the allocation result to selection error over a finite candidate set. tldr: 本文推导了稀有事件加权风险估计的精确有限总体方差并求解最优分层分配，证明类不平衡比例会在最优分配中抵消，因此均等分配优于按比例分配和简单随机抽样。
en_tdlr: This paper derives the exact finite-population variance of a weighted risk estimator and solves for the optimal stratified allocation, showing that the class-imbalance ratio cancels out, making equal allocation—rather than proportional or simple random sampling—the optimal default.
